title: A display view is recorded on load and on each display or tab switch
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser (private window) · Google Analytics DebugView access · about 15 minutes
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043). Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher).
  • Role: Owner/Admin. On a QA branch sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders). This user is the dispatcher.
  • Location: one location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  • Analytics access: you can open Google Analytics for the property the QA build reports to, at Admin > DebugView. The QA build runs analytics in debug mode, so each event appears in DebugView within a few seconds under your user. If you cannot open DebugView, the event checks in this case cannot be done by hand: write "not checked by hand" in the result comment and pass or fail on what you can see on the Work Orders page.
  • Event names to look for in DebugView: work_orders_display_view (a display was shown), work_orders_field_load and work_orders_density_load (the fields and density you have, once per display per session), work_orders_field_toggle and work_orders_density_change (a saved change).
  • Your saved display is List.
  • There are enough work orders at this location for a Tech View group or Board View column to load more cards when scrolled.

Setup

  1. Click List in the display switcher once before you start, so your saved display is List.
  2. Start a fresh analytics session: close every browser window, open a new private window and sign in.
  3. Check the setup worked: Google Analytics > Admin > DebugView opens and shows your device within a few seconds of opening any ShopView page. If it does not, carry on but write "not checked by hand" for the event checks, as the Preconditions say.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and wait for the rows to load. In DebugView, count the work_orders_display_view events.
  2. Click Tech View in the display switcher at the right of the toolbar (tooltip "Tech View").
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher (tooltip "Board View").
  4. Click the Estimates tab, then the All tab.
  5. Scroll a long column or group so more cards load, then wait 30 seconds.
  6. Type "ZZAUTOTEST" in Search, then click Status and tick "Approved".
  7. Narrow the browser window below 1024 px wide, then widen it back to full size.
  8. Count the work_orders_display_view events since step 1 and read the display and tab each one names.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: exactly 1 display view is recorded, for List on the tab you opened.
  • Steps 2 and 3: 1 more each, naming Tech View, then Board View (running total 3).
  • Step 4: 1 more for each tab switch, naming Estimates, then All (running total 5).
  • Steps 5 to 7: no new display view. Loading more rows, searching, filtering and narrowing then widening the window back to the same display and tab are not new views.
  • Step 8: total = 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 display views. The Work Orders page looked and worked as usual throughout.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10593 (Story 12, Google Analytics for display and field usage); SV-10048 (Story 5, Fields to display and columns); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S12-R1, S12-R6, S5-R7, read 8 Oct 2026. Event names and timing: SV-10593 comments by Slavcho Mitrov and Milos Vasic, 6 Oct 2026 (the agreed GA4 event table); earlier event contract on Review Decisions page 853901313 (29 Sep 2026) uses older names. Tech plan (revised 24 Sep 2026) Phase 10 tests.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S12-R1: “Measure display usage after successful initial loading and each display or filter-view switch.”
  • S12-R6: “Do not count ordinary row refreshes as new display views.”
  • S5-R7: “Measure display, field, and density usage as specified in Story 12.”
  • Tech plan Phase 10 tests refetch: “no event on refetch or continuation”
  • Story 12 prerequisites: “Reuse the application’s existing Google Analytics setup and analytics identity/consent policy. Work Orders view permission is required; field visibility follows S5-E2.”

Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.
